subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary web_fetch URLs, and if so should the approved surface be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, confirmation-based, or folded into the broader egress policy?
rationale: The low-level SSRF primitive exists, but exposing it through web_fetch changes a model-directed network security boundary and a public config contract, so automation should not choose the policy shape.

options.title: Approve a scoped dangerous SSRF policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented web_fetch ssrfPolicy design that can allow private-network access only with explicit operator intent, audit visibility, cache isolation, redirect handling, and metadata/link-local rules.

options.title: Keep only narrow fake-IP support
options.body: Leave current main as-is and document that arbitrary private-network web_fetch remains unsupported while RFC2544/ULA proxy cases stay the only opt-ins.

options.title: Fold into egress policy design
options.body: Route this through the broader web-tool egress firewall so private-network access, domain allowlists, deny rules, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped dangerous SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented web_fetch ssrfPolicy design that can allow private-network access only with explicit operator intent, audit visibility, cache isolation, redirect handling, and metadata/link-local rules.
